summary: QUORUM, all up: local apply on 10.0.0.1 (commit log then memtable) plus MUTATION_REQ to .2 and .3, blockFor 2, no hints. Only works with ks1.users input; the flow's default shop.users skips the apply (contract seam). The sim reports acks 3 because there's no early return at blockFor.
One replica down inside max_hint_window: success with 2 acks; shouldHint then submitHint then HintsService.write for 10.0.0.2.
Two replicas down: unavailable (4096, required 2, alive 1) from ReplicaPlans.forWrite before sendToHintedReplicas; no mutation sent, no hints.

write-timeout, received 1 of 2, SIMPLE, both non-responders hinted via onFailure(TIMEOUT); outcome and path reproduced. The client sees it at 4082ms, not 2000ms, because the sequential foreach adds up per-replica timeouts and timeout_ms can't be computed. Clarified: the hints come from callback expiry.

ONE with one slow replica: success and a hint for the slow replica reproduced, but success arrives at 2095ms instead of right after the local ack (no parallel fan-out or early return). Clarified: in the code the hint is written after the client response.

Corrected: with 3 nodes and RF 3 the coordinator is a replica and always alive to itself, so all replicas down needs a 4-node ring. ANY skips the liveness check; the hint counts as the single ack (blockFor 1). Minor: the model makes 3 HintRunnables where the code makes 1.
ALL with one replica down: unavailable (required 3, alive 2) before anything is sent.

Replica: commit log append (beginWrite), then memtable put, then MUTATION_RSP with no fsync wait under periodic sync; a failed append leaves the memtable untouched. Clarified: periodic mode does block when the last sync is more than 15000ms old.

Flush switches the memtable, writes an SSTable via the FlushRunnable, adds it to the live set, reclaims memory, and PostFlush discardCompletedSegments deletes the segments made unused. Clarified: segments still dirty for other tables are kept.

commitlog-replay-startup reapplies the 2 unflushed entries to the memtables without the commit log, skips the persisted one, flushes and deletes the file. daemon-startup orders replay before initServer and the native transport, but cassandra-daemon.setup hardcodes segments: [], so startup replay can't be driven. Edit: feed the segments from state (e.g. a commitlog-disk store).
